items.headline: RBI rate panel in day two; decision due October 7 with a 25 bps hike to 5.50% widely expected
items.summary: The MPC concludes tomorrow. Most economists expect the first hike since February 2023, from 5.25%. The 10-year G-Sec yield stood at 7.21% on October 5. Ongoing: expectations unchanged since last week.
items.rationale: A hike is largely priced; the statement on further tightening and the inflation forecast will move bond yields, the rupee and rate-sensitive sectors such as housing and autos.

industries.why: Home loans set to get dearer
Vehicle loans set to get dearer

economies.why: Wider rate gap supports the rupee

items.headline: Sensex rises 473 points to 72,382 as domestic funds absorb ₹4,699 crore of foreign selling
items.summary: The Sensex gained 0.66% and the Nifty 0.6% to 22,555.75, ending a four-session losing streak as crude eased and Fed hike fears faded. Foreign investors sold a net ₹4,699 crore; domestic institutions bought ₹5,182 crore. Relief, but foreign selling continues.
items.rationale: Domestic funds are cushioning foreign outflows, which limits downside, but persistent foreign selling keeps pressure on index heavyweights and the rupee.

items.headline: Rupee slips to 96.41 per dollar as oil and US yields rise, reversing Monday's gain
items.summary: The rupee opened flat at 96.31 and weakened to 96.41 as crude firmed and US Treasury yields stayed high. The RBI is expected to smooth volatility. Reverses Monday's 10-paise gain.
items.rationale: A weaker rupee raises the cost of oil and other imports and adds to imported inflation, while lifting IT and pharma exporters' rupee earnings.

items.headline: US 10-year Treasury yield hovers near 5.3%, its highest since 2002
items.summary: The 10-year yield touched a fresh 2002 high to start the week before easing to about 5.26%. It has risen about 0.46 points in a month. Ongoing.
items.rationale: High US yields draw foreign money out of Indian stocks and bonds, weaken the rupee and push up Indian bond yields.

items.headline: India's services PMI rises to 55.2 in September, a three-month high, as input cost inflation eases
items.summary: The final services PMI was 55.2, up from 54.1 but below the 55.8 flash and 56.2 expected. New business rose fastest in three months; input cost inflation fell to a 10-month low. New.
items.rationale: Firmer services demand supports earnings and jobs, while easing cost pressure helps the inflation outlook ahead of the RBI decision.

items.headline: India–US trade talks have 'reached a plateau', finance minister says; compromise 'very difficult'
items.summary: Sitharaman said further give-and-take would be very difficult, after a US law allowed tariffs of up to 100% on big buyers of Russian oil. Talks continue. Escalating from last week's reports of delays.
items.rationale: A stalled deal keeps US tariff risk hanging over Indian exporters and weighs on foreign investor sentiment and the rupee.

items.headline: Brent firms to $100.84 as Gulf and Red Sea attacks keep a risk premium despite better supply
items.summary: Brent rose 0.5% in Asian trade, reversing Monday's dip, as attacks on shipping near Yemen and Hormuz continued; crew pay near the strait has jumped. Brent is up about 3.8% in a month.
items.rationale: Crude near $100 keeps India's import bill, fuel inflation and rupee pressure high, squeezing airlines, fuel marketers and crude-linked manufacturers.

items.headline: India's LNG imports fall 14% in September; Oman becomes top supplier with a 27% share
items.summary: India imported 585,000 tonnes of LNG from Oman in September, overtaking the US, now third at 16%. Qatar's share fell after earlier damage at its main export hub. Ongoing supply diversification.
items.rationale: Lower LNG volumes tighten gas for city-gas distributors, fertiliser plants and industry, while diversification reduces dependence on the Hormuz route.

items.headline: Ship sinks in Black Sea after drone attack, three Indian crew safe; India seeks shipping-safety deal
items.summary: A Turkish-owned cargo ship sank off Romania, killing two; three Indian crew survived. India's foreign minister said New Delhi is talking to Russia and Ukraine on Black Sea shipping safety, grain and energy exports. Escalating.
items.rationale: Black Sea attacks threaten supplies of sunflower oil, grain and fertiliser that India imports; a deal brokered with India's help would ease that risk.

industries.why: Fertiliser and edible oil supply risk
